This plot is small, only a corner near the house, but maize is our food so I must treat it well. I will buy a little urea and NPK from the market if the price is not too high, and I will also carry goat and chicken droppings from our compound to spread before planting. The seed I will use is the one my neighbour gave me from last harvest — the improved seed from the agro-dealer is too costly for such a small piece, and I am intercropping with cowpea and melon as we always do. No borehole here, so we wait for the rain, and my wife and children will help with weeding; I will only call two or three young men from the village when it is time to clear and ridge.
